summary: Shizuka Sasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Jikido Takasaki at Kyoto University, as well as at UC Berkeley and Bukkyo University. At Hanazono University, he served as lecturer (1990), assistant professor (1992), and professor (2002).

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) specialized in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (Promotion 1926–1934). He taught at the University of Paris and the Institut d'Histoire des Sciences et des Techniques, and was a philosophy professor at Hebrew University (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1918–1921) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1921–1924), and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010, an attested lecturer at Otani University in 2012, and an attested professor at Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University, attested between 1995 and 2013.

Shodo Harada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Shofuku-ji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamakami (born 1939) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (completing doctoral credits by 1964), he served at Kyoto Sangyo University as assistant professor (attested 1979–1988) and professor (attested 1995).

Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. He served as professor at Toyo University (attested 2003–2015) and holds attested posts at Taisho University and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (2026).

Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010) and founded Sanshin Zen Community and Pioneer Valley Zendo.
Shoichi Ozawa (1929–2012) worked in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University and held a post at The Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, later serving there as assistant professor (attested 1980–1981) and professor (attested 1995–1998). He was also a researcher at the Okurayama Institute.

Shoji Muramoto works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Zurich. He held posts at Hanazono University and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, where he was Professor of Foreign Studies (attested 2002–2009).
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1962) and as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando (1928–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Ueno Gakuen University and Otani University.

Shokin Furuta (1911–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Tokyo University and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He was a professor at Hokkaido (~1960–1964) and Nihon (~1964–1982) universities, and directed Matsugaoka Bunko from 1966.
Shoko Kanaoka (1930–2004) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Toyo University (attested in 1987 and 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Taisho University (1948–1955), where he later served as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata holds attested lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies as of 2026.
Shoko Takeuchi (1910–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University, where he later became an emeritus professor (attested 1987–1995).

Shoko Watanabe (1907–1977) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history scholar. He studied under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969).
